questions.question: Which change alone is NOT enough to overload a method?
options: Changing the type of a parameter
Changing the order of parameter types
questions.explanation: The signature is the name plus parameter list. Return type is not part of it, so a return-type-only change is a duplicate.

questions.question: void go(long x) { print("long"); } void go(Integer x) { print("Integer"); } ... go(5); What prints?
questions.explanation: Widening int to long happens in the first phase, before boxing to Integer is even considered.

questions.question: void tap(Integer x) { print("box"); } void tap(int... x) { print("var"); } ... tap(7); What prints?
questions.explanation: Boxing is tried in the second phase, before varargs in the third, so tap(Integer) wins.

questions.question: class Meter { int read(int a) { return a; } double read(int a) { return a; } } Why does this fail?
options: read(int) is already defined in the class
questions.explanation: Both methods have the signature read(int). A different return type does not make them different.

questions.question: When is the overloaded method to call chosen?
options: At runtime, based on the object
questions.explanation: Overload resolution is done by the compiler using the declared argument types, which is why it is static polymorphism.

questions.question: void fee(int a, long b) { } void fee(long a, int b) { } ... fee(5, 5); What happens?
options: Compile error: reference to fee is ambiguous
questions.explanation: Each method needs one widening, so neither is more specific. The compiler refuses to guess.

questions.question: Can the main method be overloaded?
options: Yes, but the JVM still starts from main(String[] args)
Yes, and the JVM picks the one with fewest parameters
Only if the class is abstract
questions.explanation: Extra main versions are ordinary overloads. The JVM only looks for public static void main(String[]).

questions.question: void show(int... v) { System.out.print(v.length); } ... show(); show(4, 9); What prints?
questions.explanation: A varargs method accepts zero arguments as an empty array (length 0), then two arguments (length 2).

questions.question: void note(String s) { } void note(Integer i) { } ... note(null); What happens?
questions.explanation: null fits both reference types and neither is more specific. A cast such as (String) null fixes it.

questions.question: Which pair of methods is a valid overload?
options: void tag(int count) and void tag(int size)
int tag(int a) and long tag(int a)
void tag(int a) and static void tag(int a)
void tag(int a, String b) and void tag(String b, int a)
questions.explanation: Different order of parameter types gives a different signature. Names, return types and static do not.
